title: Signed Hom short-complex comparison with an opposite total
statement: Let (C,J,R) be a ringed site [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and let E,A be integer-indexed cochain complexes of module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let K be a commuting double cochain complex in the opposite category of module sheaves [def-sp-double-complex-total], with a total complex. Suppose isomorphisms e_(p,q): K^(p,q) ≅ op Hom(E^p,A^(-q)) identify the horizontal differential with the opposite of precomposition by d_E and the vertical differential with the opposite of postcomposition by d_A, for all indices. For every integer n, the short complex at n of the product Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] is isomorphic to the unop of the short complex at -n of Tot(K). No exactness, boundedness, freeness, or sheafification hypothesis is required.

source.place: Section 0A8X, product Hom complex and signed differential; Tags 0GM7/0GM8, Hom calculation. Opposite-total comparison is the agent-written coordinate calculation below.

proof.text: Obtain the product projections and their limiting and differential specifications from homComplex_projections_exists. Construct the signed degree map as the unop of K.totalDesc, whose (p,q) component is e_(p,q) followed by the opposite of the Hom projection multiplied by (p*n+p*(p+1)/2).negOnePow. Construct the inverse by Fan.IsLimit.lift, using the total coprojection at (p,-(p+n)), the inverse of e, and the same sign. The total coprojection identity and product projection identity prove both composites are identities; the square of every integer unit is one. This gives degreewise isomorphisms with the stated signed projection formula, without boundedness.

Check differential compatibility after unop every total coprojection. Expand the total differential using ι_D₁, ι_D₂, d₁_eq and d₂_eq. Apply the signed projection formulas and unop the hypotheses h₁,h₂. Expand the Hom differential using homComplex_projections_exists. The coefficients agree because the triangular integer expression satisfies (p+1)*(p+2)/2 = p*(p+1)/2+p+1, proved by ring and omega over all integers, and negOnePow_add and negOnePow_succ give the horizontal and vertical sign identities. The remaining additive equality is abel. Total.hom_ext proves the differential square.

Use ShortComplex.isoMk on the degree isomorphisms at n-1,n,n+1 and the two differential squares. Transport from explicitly indexed short complexes to canonical sc by HomologicalComplex.isoSc' and the opposite short-complex functor. This gives the asserted isomorphism at n, including zero and unbounded complexes.

theorem homComplex_sc_iso_dual_total
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
    {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}}
    (E A : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{w}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})).obj R)) ℤ)
    (K : HomologicalComplex₂ (SheafOfModules.{max u v w}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})).obj R))ᵒᵖ
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    [K.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ)]
    (e : ∀ p q : ℤ, (K.X p).X q ≅ op (SheafOfModules.homObj (E.X p) (A.X (-q))))
    (h₁ : ∀ p p' q : ℤ,
      (K.d p p').f q ≫ (e p' q).hom = (e p q).hom ≫
        (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (E.d p p') (𝟙 (A.X (-q)))).op)
    (h₂ : ∀ p q q' : ℤ,
      (K.X p).d q q' ≫ (e p q').hom = (e p q).hom ≫
        (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (𝟙 (E.X p)) (A.d (-q') (-q))).op)
    (n : ℤ) :
    Nonempty ((CategoryTheory.homComplex E A).sc n ≅
      ((K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).sc (-n)).unop)
